text:
Sam H: Quick proposal for svc-to-svc contract shape — thinking we standardize on canonical protobufs in repo, serve internal gRPC, and expose HTTP/2 + protojson at the gateway (transcoding JSON <-> proto). Gateway does content negotiation. Ping @Vivian for client concerns.

Vivian L: Why not gRPC everywhere? Browsers + some mobile SDKs struggle with pure gRPC (need grpc-web). Adds complexity on client side.

Sam H: Yep. Browser compatibility is the main reason. Also easier onboarding for external partners if we offer JSON. The idea: proto is the source of truth, servers implement gRPC; envoy/nginx does transcoding at ingress for JSON clients.

Mohit R: Telemetry question: when we transcode we lose the original wire proto representation. For tracing and regression tests we need a way to map back to proto fields reliably. Proposing we add a header `x-rw-proto-version` + include `x-rw-proto-checksum` so post-ingest we can assert fidelity.

Katie P: Risk for rollouts: transcoding semantics can subtly change defaults/unknown field handling. We need a canary plan: opt-in transcode for 5-10% traffic and a golden test set to validate parity before full rollout. Also surface transcode mismatches in the console.

Jordan: Performance/ops note — envoy transcoding is CPU-heavy for large payloads. Gateway could become a hotspot. Options: (a) dedicated transcoding pool (separate service), (b) offload to our dedicated runtime (Redwood runtime) with accelerated kernels, or (c) only allow transcode for small/idl payloads. We should measure cost.

Sam H: Minimal example for discussion:
```proto
syntax = "proto3";
package usersvc;

message CreateUser {
  string name = 1;
  string email = 2;
}

service User {
  rpc Create(CreateUser) returns (UserRecord);
}
```
curl example: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/users -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"name":"alex","email":"a@x.com"}'`
Gateway would transcode that JSON into proto and call internal gRPC.

Vivian L: :thinking: What about streaming RPCs? Server streaming / bidi stream doesn't map cleanly to JSON over simple HTTP. grpc-web handles some cases but browsers are still tricky. Maybe mark streaming RPCs as gRPC-only and require gateway to return 422 if requested JSON path maps to a streaming endpoint.

Mohit R: Agree on streaming. For telemetry we should tag requests with `x-rw-contract: protojson-v1` and emit a `transcoded=true` flag in logs so dashboards can filter. Also preserve `x-request-id` across gateway <-> backend.

Katie P: Console UX reqs: per-route contract version, per-route transcode toggle, and a quick health panel showing "transcode-error-rate" and 95th latency for transcode stage. Also a rollout button that toggles transcode percentage with an automated smoke test.

Jordan: Ops suggestion: implement stage that validates proto parity on canary traffic by calling both paths (direct gRPC and transcoded gateway) and doing strict diff on response proto. If diffs > threshold, auto-roll back canary. That will catch defaulting/round-trip issues.

deploy-bot: deploy completed: transpiler-service:v2 -> canary 10% (region: us-west-2) :rocket:

Sam H: Good next steps: I'll draft short RFC with listed tradeoffs (client compatibility, streaming, telemetry, perf) and include envoy example config + canary playbook. Will add a sample test harness to repo that diffs proto outputs.

Vivian L: +1 

Mohit R: +1 on adding `x-rw-proto-checksum` and `transcoded` logs.

Katie P: I'll draft the console UX for the rollout button + metrics tiles and link in the RFC.

Jordan: I'll add perf numbers for envoy transcoding vs dedicated pool in the RFC.

Sam H: Thanks everyone — filing RFC today. :thumbsup:
